holidays.name: National Raspberry Cream Pie Day
holidays.description: A day to enjoy tart raspberries and silky cream in a flaky crust. Bake one, buy one, or split a slice with a friend while raspberries are at their peak.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It lines up with late-summer raspberry season, which makes the timing sensible.
holidays.funFact: The first recorded recipe for raspberry cream pie dates to 1896, so people have been eating it for well over a century.

holidays.name: Lammas Day
holidays.description: An old harvest festival that marks the first cut of the grain crop. Traditionally, people baked loaves from the first wheat of the season and brought them to be blessed.
holidays.origin: Lammas has roots in early English tradition. The name comes from the Old English for 'loaf mass', and the day was kept as a thanksgiving for the first fruits of the harvest.
holidays.funFact: The word 'Lammas' literally means 'loaf mass', which makes it one of the few holidays named after bread.

holidays.name: Spider-Man Day
holidays.description: A day for web-slinger fans to rewatch the movies, reread the comics, or just hang upside down in tribute to your friendly neighborhood hero.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial fan observance for the Marvel superhero. Its date is generally tied to the August 1962 cover date of Amazing Fantasy #15, which introduced Spider-Man.
holidays.funFact: Spider-Man first appeared on the cover of Amazing Fantasy #15, the final issue of that comic series, and he went on to become one of the most popular superheroes in the world.
